newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage rates at lowest levels in more than a year.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage rates at lowest levels in more than a year.

text.p: U.S. mortgage rates fell this week to their lowest levels in more than a year, Freddie Mac said Thursday.

Thirty-year mortgage rates averaged 7.36 percent in the week ending Aug.1 from 7.43 percent last week. This is the lowest rate since the week ended Feb. 23, 1996, when the mortgage was available at 7.32 percent.
Fifteen-year mortgage rates fell to 6.90 percent from 6.98 percent. The rate has never been this low since the week ended March 8, 1996, when it hit 6.96 percent.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates fell to 5.49 percent in the week from 5.54 last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.23 percent, the 15-year 7.75 percent and the adjustable rate 5.98 percent.

The fall in interest rates can be attributed to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony last week that growth is slowing, as well as to the tentative budget accord reached by Democrats and Republicans, Freddie Mac chief economist Robert Van Order said.

"Interest rates dropped this week partly in response to Fed Chairman Greenspan's optimistic remarks of last week, but also as a result of news of the upcoming federal budget agreement," Van Order said.
"The budget agreement news may well carry over into next week, bringing us interest rates that are even more affordable than they are now."
Fees and points charged by lenders for 30-year and 15-year loans were unchanged from last week at an average 1.7 percent. Adjustable loan charges also held steady at 1.4 percent.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
